title: Honey Vanilla Bean Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla bean cupcakes sweetened with wildflower honey, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes use real vanilla bean specks and wildflower honey instead of plain sugar syrup. The honey adds a floral sweetness that plain vanilla cupcakes do not have. I tested this batch three times in my home kitchen until the crumb stayed soft the next day. The frosting is a silky honey buttercream, not too sweet, with a light floral finish that matches the cake.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat the softened butter, honey, and sugar together for 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each one.
Mix in the vanilla bean seeds and vanilla extract.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with the milk. Mix just until combined.
Divide the batter evenly between the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For the frosting, beat the butter until smooth. Add the honey and beat for 1 minute.
Add the powdered sugar in two parts, then the vanilla and salt. Beat for 2 more minutes until silky.
Once the cupcakes are fully cool, pipe or spread the frosting on top.
tips: Split the vanilla bean lengthwise and scrape the seeds with the back of a knife for the most specks.
Use room temperature eggs and milk so the batter mixes smoothly and rises evenly.
Warm the honey for 10 seconds in the microwave before measuring, so it pours easily.
If the frosting looks too soft, chill it for 10 minutes, then beat again before piping.

faq.question: Can I use a vanilla bean paste instead of a whole bean?
faq.answer: Yes, use 1 tablespoon of vanilla bean paste in place of one scraped bean. You will lose some of the visible specks but keep the flavor.

faq.question: Why did my honey cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: Overmixing after adding the flour is the main cause. Mix just until you no longer see streaks of flour.

faq.question: Can I swap wildflower honey for another type?
faq.answer: Clover or orange blossom honey both work well. Avoid very dark honey like buckwheat, since it can taste bitter in this cake.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store them in a sealed container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or in the fridge for up to 5 days.

conclusion: These honey vanilla bean cupcakes prove that simple ingredients can still taste special. The real vanilla bean and wildflower honey turn a basic cake into something worth making again. Bake a batch this weekend and see how the honey frosting wins over your family.
